versions.changelog: Authorization links now carry source attribution (host / distribution channel / skill / version) so conversions can be attributed per channel. No additional user data is collected — everything is derived from the script's own install path.

Lead with browser sign-in when no credential is present; only fall back to API keys for CI/server environments. Corrected database provenance (CALCD = China Automotive Life Cycle Database, CATARC x HiQ; HiQLCD-AL built with the China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association).

Removed the four methodology reference files; search and dataset selection run server-side. Corrected database provenance: CALCD is the China Automotive Life Cycle Database (CATARC x HiQ); HiQLCD-AL is the aluminium industry database built with the China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association.

Adds browser sign-in — no API key required.

- `python3 scripts/cortex.py login` runs an RFC 8628 device flow: one click in the browser, then the credential is stored locally (mode 600) and every command works. Visible data matches the user's own account, including any licensed commercial databases.
- The flow is three plain HTTP calls, documented in SKILL.md — any agent that can run shell commands can perform it without the bundled script and without installing a CLI.
- Credential layer now picks the right header automatically (API key vs signed-in credential); the gateway detects the type, so callers supply one of the two and nothing else.
- Troubleshooting: polling 428 is the normal pending state; signing in swaps the credential but does not grant entitlements.

Fixed: login output was block-buffered on non-tty, so the authorization URL was invisible when the output was piped or redirected.

Major update from 1.3.0.

Critical fix: the MCP tools documented in 1.3.0 (search_lca_data, run_cortex) were retired server-side and now return "Unknown tool"; the example dataset keys used an obsolete format and resolve to missing. This release matches the current API.

Added
- Dual access path: use the native MCP tools when the host supports them, otherwise a bundled stdlib-only Python script (no pip install, no config file edits). The skill tells the agent how to detect which is available and how to set up the other.
- Seven data operations: dataset details, GWP cohort distribution with percentile positioning, non-GWP LCIA indicators, process-stage hotspots, published-EPD search, EPD peer distribution and outlier fences.
- Entitlement tiers: 11 free databases work with any valid key; commercial databases return a purchase link instead of an error, and substituting a value from another database is explicitly forbidden.
- Reference files on material families, database selection, comparability gates, and benchmarking/estimation methods.
- HITL discipline: search first, compare second, ask last.
- About and Privacy & Security sections.

Fixed in the bundled script: default user-agent blocked by the CDN; percentile positioning printing None; --json rejected after the subcommand; internal sentinel links that users cannot open.
Major update: privacy statement, MCP config moved up, improved description, example output, expanded When to Use triggers, more tags
Homepage back to hiqlcd.com; add Cortex web app as browser-based alternative in integration table
Add Cortex web app and CarbonX platform links; update homepage to carbonx.hiqlcd.com/cortex
Add HiQ platform overview, database coverage, MCP/API integration guide, and contact info
Improve description for ClawHub display; add homepage, author, tags
Update API endpoints to x.hiqlcd.com; ask.js uses MCP run_cortex; gateway auto-injects auth

Initial public release offering comprehensive LCA dataset search and sustainability Q&A features.

- Search 40,000+ LCA datasets for carbon footprint and emission factors from Ecoinvent, HiQLCD, and CarbonMinds.
- Query and interpret GWP (Global Warming Potential) and environmental impact data by material or process.
- Natural language assistant supports explanations, comparisons, calculations, and research in LCA and sustainability.
- Includes guidance for setup, API key configuration, and CLI usage.
- Coverage for major LCA standards (ISO 14040/44) and key industry terms.
- Clear documentation on when to use the skill for best results.
